QUESTION OF THE WEEK - After last week's 50 basis point rate cut in official interest to 6.50 percent, economists were asked about the probability of another easing in this cycle, when it would likely take place, and by how much. With some sections of

the market having been looking for a larger easing this week, some analysts feel there is already a case for rates to be lowered again given that inflation is expected to remain subdued and that the economy is showing signs of going nowhere fast.
Others feel it will very much depend on the data flow over the coming weeks, particularly the capitial expenditure and enterprise bargaining agreements reports due later this month.

However, the general concensus is that if there is going to be another easing, it will be by a further 50 basis points in the first quarter of next year and probably after the December quarter inflation and wages data which are released in February.
Housing Finance Chance of When Size

HOUSING FINANCE - Analysts generally expect a healthy rise in commitments in September, reflecting the lagged impact of two rounds of mortgage rate cuts in June and July and the 0.5 point easing in official policy on July 31. Many felt the most

important feature would be commitments for the construction of new dwellings, seen as a bellwether of trends in the housing market. Another rise in this measure would confirm assumptions the market was staging a slow recovery after almost three years of weakness. They were also interested to see if growth in mortgage refinancing showed some sign of slowing after accounting for a record number of commitments in August.
